newsitem.title: GREECE: OLYMPIC AIRWAYS "GO SLOW" STRANDS SCORES OF TOURISTS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPIC AIRWAYS "GO SLOW" STRANDS SCORES OF TOURISTS.

text.p: Scores of tourists were stranded at Athens' airport on Monday as a result of a "go slow" by Olympic Aviation engineers, affecting many flights to the popular Greek holiday islands.
Airport officials said at least 20 flights were cancelled or delayed for up to four hours with passengers crammed inside the old airport's premises or standing outside in sizzling heat.

"This is rediculous. I have been waiting for my flight to be announced for the past three hours. I was hoping to get to an island with my wife and daughter for a nice vacation in Greece but got off to a very bad start," said British tourist Ian Donovan.
"If Greece wants us to come here and spend our money then it should at least make sure it provides basic services like regular flights to tourist locations," his wife Margaret, said.
Olympic Aviation is a subsidiary of the state-owned Olympic Airways serving the popular Aegean Sea islands visited by thousands of tourists each summer.

"The network to the islands is seriously affected by the mechanics' action," a senior government official told Reuters. "It gives Greece a bad name abroad and deals a blow in our efforts to upgrade our tourism services."
The mechanics have banned overtime and demand instead that Olympic, which is deeply in the red, hires more staff.
Olympic Aviation's board was meeting all-day on Monday to deal with the situation and officials said that flights to the islands would be reduced over the next two weeks.

Popular island destinations including Paros, Mykonos, Santorini, Skiathos, Zakynthos, Milos and Chios would be affected and hotel owners expressed fears that room reservations from abroad would be cancelled.
The mechanics said that during the busy summer season they are forced to work an average five hours overtime per day under difficult conditions.
Tourism minister Vasso Papandreou made a plea to the mechanics to stop their action saying it threatened to seriously damage the tourist season.

"We are working our normal eight-hour shifts in order to press for the hiring of seasonal staff who are necessary for maintaining the normal flights schedule," said Theodosis Arbatzoglou, president of Olympic's mechanics union.
A number of foreign carriers warned Greece last summer that they would reduce flights to Athens' airport due to long delays, then caused by an antiquated radar system.
